subject: GO TO statement
notes: kb/Work/PB412.md landed w41. PDF page 660 (printed folio 630) re-rendered at 190 dpi, the diagram being load-bearing: Format 1 is 'GO TO procedure-name-1' with only GO underlined, so TO is an optional word (5.2.3) and procedure-name-1 is unbracketed and therefore singular and required (5.2.6.2); Format 2 is 'GO TO { procedure-name-1 } ... DEPENDING ON identifier-1' -- one or more names (5.2.7), DEPENDING underlined and required (5.2.2), ON optional. The transcription matches the page. THE REPAIR IS STRUCTURAL: goToStatement now carries ONE ALTERNATIVE PER PRINTED FORMAT plus the edition-gated ANSI-85 target-less arm, so the complement is a syntax error in the parser; GoToFormats.Of is the ONE classifier every reader asks (the binder's total three-arm switch, the BareGotoRemoved2002 gate, and the ALTER sole-GO-TO-paragraph test), replacing three separate reconstructions from optional children; and CobolErrorStrategy re-codes the resulting parse error as COBOL2172 naming the format's own cardinalities. WHAT WAS WRONG: the rule was the single union 'GO TO? procedureName? (procedureName)* (DEPENDING ON? dataReference)?', so 'GO TO A B.' compiled at every edition and the Format-1 bind arm read names[0] and DISCARDED B in silence, while 'GO TO DEPENDING ON X.' compiled clean and aborted the run unit on a BoundUnsupported loud stage -- that stage is now deleted. Measured after the fix: both shapes refused with COBOL2172 at 85/2002/2014/2023, the bare form still gated by name (COBOL0811) at 2002+ and accepted at 85, and the six legal spellings (TO omitted, ON omitted, one and three procedure-names, a section target, a qualified name) plus GR2's out-of-range fall-through all correct.
